title: Geometry-Aware Score-Repellent Monte Carlo
topic: Probabilistic Methods->Monte Carlo and Sampling Methods
claim: Proposal-side and repulsion-side geometry are complementary: combining both gives the most balanced sampling efficiency across anisotropic coordinates.
layout: 5 columns by 3 rows, left-to-right comparison, ESS annotations in each panel
description: A 5-column by 3-row grid compares samplers: MALA, FisherMALA, MALA+GA-SRMC, FisherMALA+SRMC and FisherMALA+GA-SRMC. The top row, labeled 'one step', is a schematic on a 2-D anisotropic Gaussian. It shows a black ellipse for the true level set and red or green dashed ellipses for the surrogate targets. Blue proposal-noise blobs, orange and black score arrows and a dotted 'recent history' cloud sit near the current point. Small colored tags mark the proposal type and the tilt: gray for none, red for SRMC, green for GA-SRMC. The middle row shows viridis-colored density contours with sample scatter, start and end stars, and accuracy and ESS numbers for x1 and x2. The bottom row shows noisy coordinate trace plots for x1 and x2 over iterations. A shared legend sits between the top and middle rows. The eye goes first to the column titles and then to the ESS numbers.
caption: Proposal-side and repulsion-side geometry are complementary. Top: one-step mechanism. The preconditioner A shapes proposal movements, while the GA-SRMC matrix M shapes the history-dependent surrogate target. Middle/bottom: samples and coordinate paths on an anisotropic Gaussian target. Combining FisherMALA with GA-SRMC yields the most balanced effective sample sizes (ESS) across coordinates, computed from N = 1000 post-burn-in samples with ESS estimation in Geyer [25]. Full setup and details are deferred to Appendix A.1.
abstract: The recently proposed Score-Repellent Monte Carlo (SRMC) method improves MCMC sampling by tilting the target density $Ï$ in $\mathbb{R}^d$ with the factor $\exp(-Î±\,Î¸_n^\top s(x))$, where the score function $s(x) = \nabla_x \log Ï(x)$, and $Î¸_n$ is the score average from past samples. However, a single scalar repellence strength $Î±\ge0$ cannot handle both the steep and the flat directions in anisotropic energy landscapes at once. We introduce \emph{Geometry-Aware SRMC} (GA-SRMC), which generalizes the Euclidean alignment to $Î¸^\top M s(x)$ for any symmetric positive-definite matrix $M$. A stochastic-approximation central limit theorem under a trace constraint on $M$ identifies the trace-normalized inverse Fisher $M_{\rm opt}\propto S^{-1}$ as the unique minimizer of the worst-direction covariance bound, elevating the Fisher information $S=\text{Cov}_Ï(s,s)$ from a proposal-side preconditioner (e.g., FisherMALA, natural gradient) to the bound-optimal repulsion-side matrix, with a single online estimate $\widehat S_n$ serving both roles at no additional computational cost. The full-Fisher online metric $M_n$ converges almost surely to $M_{\rm opt}$ and satisfies a CLT, providing a theoretical guarantee for the online implementation of the GA-SRMC framework. On an $8$-target simulation spanning the condition number $Îº\in[1.3,100]$ and dimension $d\in[2,785]$, GA-SRMC dominates SRMC in ESS by $\boldsymbol{4.3\times}$ on anisotropic Gaussian ($Îº=100$) and $\boldsymbol{6.8\times}$ on MNIST under the MALA baseline, by $\boldsymbol{16\text{--}32\%}$ on three well-conditioned logistic-regression posteriors, and by up to $\boldsymbol{+48\%}$ under FisherMALA; gains peak on the most anisotropic targets, and posterior-mean MSE is lower than with SRMC in all $16$ full-Fisher implementations.
